name: Candidate narrates shipped-to-prod evidence — portfolio_absent_for_claim suppressed at product-grade archetype

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I'm Aarav, final-year CSE at IIT Bombay, CGPA 8.6, zero backlogs.

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: Walk me through your strongest project.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I built a campus payments reconciliation tool — FastAPI backend, Postgres, Redis for the idempotency cache. We deployed it to production last semester and it's been live for 4 months now serving roughly 1,200 weekly active students across the hostel mess and cafeteria. The repo is internal to the institute so I can't share it publicly, but the deployment is real and the merged PRs went through code review by the institute IT team.

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: What was the hardest design call you made on that project?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Choosing the idempotency window. We had to make sure a retry from the mobile app wouldn't double-charge a student if the network flaked mid-confirm. I went with a 24-hour Redis key on the request hash plus a unique constraint on the orders table — defence in depth so a Redis miss still wouldn't double-write.

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: How would you approach finding the longest substring without repeating characters?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Sliding window — left and right pointer, a hashmap of char to last-seen index. When you see a repeat, advance left to one past the last seen index of the repeating char. Track max length as you go. O(n) time, O(min(n, alphabet)) space.

transcript.speaker: ai
transcript.text: What's your CGPA and any backlogs?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: 8.6, no active or history of backlogs.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Two — what's the typical first-year scope for a backend fresher on the payments-core team, and how does on-call rotation work for freshers in the first 6 months?
